<text:style bold="true">Raster Tools</text:style>

<image:base64 col="0" width="23" wrap="none"></image:base64>

The Raster Tools work on a raster picture (a pasted picture or an opened PNG, BMP,
JPG or WEBP): select the picture first, otherwise the buttons are grayed (they are
active when a raster picture is among the selected objects). Selections are objects
of the drawing, tied to the picture: they appear as a dashed figure and can be
changed or deleted like any other object.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Rectangular selection</text:style>
Drag on the picture to select a rectangle of pixels. Shift adds the new
selection to the one that is there; Shift+Ctrl subtracts it from it. If the new selection overlaps the old ones, they are joined into one outline (their union).<text:style bold="true"> Active</text:style>
       <text:style bold="true">when:</text:style> a raster picture is among the selected objects; otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Elliptical selection</text:style>
Drag the box of an ellipse on the picture. Shift adds, Shift+Ctrl subtracts.<text:style bold="true"></text:style>
<text:style bold="true">Active when:</text:style> a raster picture is among the selected objects; otherwise it is
       grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Freehand selection</text:style>
Draw around the area that you want, holding the mouse button.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a
raster picture is among the selected objects; otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Magic wand</text:style>
Click a point of the picture: the area of a similar colour becomes a
selection (Shift adds it to the selection, Shift+Ctrl subtracts it). How
       similar is set by the Tolerance field (in the bar at the bottom and in the
       properties of the selection, where it can still be changed).<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a
       raster picture is among the selected objects; otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Selection from a figure</text:style>
Click a closed figure that lies on the picture: the figure becomes the
selection.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a raster picture is among the selected objects;
       otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Clone</text:style>
The clone stamp. Ctrl+click the place to copy from, then paint where the copy
goes. Its width and the feather (the copy fades towards the border of the
       stroke) are in the properties.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a raster picture is among the
       selected objects; otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Eraser</text:style>
Paint over the picture with the secondary colour: it is left behind where the brush
passes. If the secondary colour is not fully opaque (see its opacity) the old
colour is not completely covered, it shows through; if there is no secondary colour
the picture becomes transparent. The primary colour is the one that is not touched:
the pixels of that colour, and of the colours near it within the Tolerance, resist
the eraser (choose None as primary colour to protect nothing). The width and the
feather (the effect fades towards the border of the brush) are in the properties,
the tolerance in the properties and in the bar at the bottom. If the picture has a
selection of pixels the eraser works only inside it. A whole stroke is undone with
a single Ctrl+Z.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a raster picture is among the selected objects;
       otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Invert selection</text:style>
The area of the raster that is selected becomes the one that is not, and the other way
round: a rectangle selected in the middle becomes a frame around it. With nothing selected
on the picture it selects everything. Pressing it again goes back. The new selection can
be filled, cut or moved as any other, and more selections can be added to it or taken
from it.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a raster picture (or one of its selections) is selected;
       otherwise it is grayed.

Selections work as in Paint: a new selection replaces the old one (a click without
dragging takes it away), and the tool stays active. The selections of a raster follow it when the
raster is moved, resized or turned. Drag inside the selected area to
move its pixels: they leave the secondary colour in their place (a transparent hole
if there is none) and become a raster of their own. With Ctrl held when the drag
starts the pixels are copied and the original stays. Press Enter, while the moved
pixels are still selected, to print them on the raster they came from: the raster
grows if they lie beyond its borders. Shift adds a new selection to the area,
Shift+Ctrl subtracts it; selections of the same picture together are the area that
is selected. The arrow keys move a selection one pixel at a time (ten with Shift):
the first press lifts the pixels, as a drag does, and the next ones move them (a key kept held down is undone by Ctrl+Z as a single step). A
selection has no handles and its outline cannot be moved or deformed: to resize,
turn or deform the selected pixels, double-click anywhere inside the selection; the
pixels become a raster of their own and the handles of the second mode (the round
one turns it) appear; while they wait for Enter (which prints them on the raster) a light dashed outline marks them while they are still where they were (also when they are not selected); it goes away as soon as they are moved, resized or turned. To apply a filter to a raster select it (or a selection of
pixels on it) and choose Filters > Apply to the selected raster: the filter of the
library is run on the pixels (a window asks for its values, if it has any, and the
raster shows the effect while you move the sliders; Cancel leaves it as it was) and
Ctrl+Z undoes it; with a selection of pixels selected the filter works only inside
it. Enter works also on any raster that lies over another raster: with the raster
selected, it is printed on the raster it overlaps (which grows if needed); if it
overlaps two or more rasters, a window asks which one to use.

A click with the right button inside the selected area offers: copy the pixels, cut
them (the selection disappears with the pixels), move them (they become a raster of their own) fill the selection with the
secondary colour (also Shift+Delete; with the secondary colour on none the pixels become transparent) and convert it to a vectorial figure (a
polygon that follows its outline; a path of straight sides if the area has holes). In its properties, "Transparent
content" makes the selected pixels transparent.


When a raster picture is dragged near a border of the image it is attracted by it and
sticks to it (magnetism of about 8 pixels on the screen). The arrow keys of the keyboard
move it freely, without magnetism.
